Body mass of Palmer penguins by species and sex

A worked example of the R analysis project template

Data: Gorman, Williams and Fraser (2014), datasets::penguins

How much heavier are males, and does it depend on the species?

Penguins measured

344 penguins, three species

Palmer Archipelago, 2007 to 2009

Analysed

333 with every measurement and a sex

Left out: 6 Adelie and 5 Gentoo

Data: datasets::penguins, shipped with R since 4.5; Gorman, Williams and Fraser (2014).

Males are heavier in every species

333 penguins. Points: individual penguins. Black: means with 95% confidence intervals.

The difference is largest in Gentoo penguins

Adelie

675 g 146 penguins

95% CI 573 to 776 g

Chinstrap

412 g 68 penguins

95% CI 254 to 570 g

Gentoo

805 g 119 penguins

95% CI 697 to 913 g

Male minus female mean body mass within each species, with a Welch confidence interval (CI).

Adjusted for species, males are heavier by 668 g

Comparison Difference (g) 95% CI (g)
Males vs females 668 599 to 736
Chinstrap vs Adelie 27 −65 to 118
Gentoo vs Adelie 1378 1301 to 1455

Linear model of body mass on species and sex; 333 penguins; R² 0.85. Chinstrap and Adelie penguins of the same sex do not clearly differ.

One difference for all species: the model assumes it, while within species the difference ranges from 412 to 805 g.
